transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-24
Start time (UTC): 15:00
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Marcus Chen (Redwood SE), Aya Singh (Redwood ML), Rachel Kim (Parcelly ML Lead), Tom Alvarez (Parcelly Infra), Priya Gupta (Parcelly PM), Nick Foster (Parcelly SRE)

Summary:
Quick check-in on the INT8/FP8 pilot segmentation results across traffic classes. Review of quality deltas by prompt bucket, p50/p95/p99 latency changes, discussion of SLA implications and canary/rollout options. Align on next steps: artifact handoff, longer throughput run, security deep-dive.

Topics covered:
- Per-bucket quality impact (snr-like scores and human evals)
- Observed perf deltas (throughput and latency percentiles)
- Batching + KV cache behavior differences between FP8 and INT8 builds
- Fallback strategies and canary rollouts for production SLA
- Security/integration asks (KMS, audit logs, VPC)

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena Ortiz: alright everyone, hi thanks for joining, uh we wanted to keep this to 45 so we can get through the per-bucket numbers and action items. Rachel you mentioned you had some new prompt buckets to show?
[00:12] Rachel Kim: yeah thanks Lena. um first quick context — the pilot ran over the last 4 days, mixed traffic from our mobile agents and web, about 20% heavy conversational agents and 80% read-only summarization. we segmented by prompt length and by intent class so we could see where INT8 is hurting quality.
[00:30] Marcus Chen: cool, when you say the pilot ran -- what was the steady-state rps we hit?
[00:34] Rachel Kim: around 220 rps peak, sustained 150 rps average. Tom can confirm infra numbers.
[00:42] Tom Alvarez: yep copy, VMs in us-east-1, we used your dedicated test pool with 8xA100 equiv, sustained token throughput was about 1.9x on the INT8 build versus baseline FP16, and cost per token looked ~35% lower in our cost model, ballpark.
[01:01] Aya Singh: important to call out that the FP8 runs gave similar throughput gains but with slightly different latency tail behavior — FP8 p95 actually trended slightly lower than INT8 on short prompts, interestingly.
[01:17] Priya Gupta: okay but quality — where did we see regressions? Rachel?
[01:21] Rachel Kim: so per our eval spreadsheet and the human spot checks: overall SNR-ish metric dropped 0.8% for FP8 on the open-domain chat bucket, INT8 dropped 2.6% averaged across the same bucket. the big delta is in the "instruction-following" long-context prompts — INT8 produced off-by-one hallucinations and occasional repetition on about 4% of the long-seq samples.
[01:46] Marcus Chen: and are those failures recoverable via calibration? like increasing layer norm epsilon, or switching KV cache precision at runtime?
[01:53] Rachel Kim: we tried the layer-norm tweak and a mitigating decode temperature adjustment; that reduced the repetition but didn't fully close the gap. we saw best improvement by using a mixed-precision KV cache for the top-most layers in INT8, kept logits in FP16 — that cut the failure rate roughly in half.
[02:14] Nick Foster: from an SRE perspective the p99 latency spikes were concerning when requests queued during bursts. Did Redwood's runtime change batching thresholds?
[02:23] Marcus Chen: we left batching policy at medium auto-batch. but on INT8 the per-token compute was lower so the batch-formation timing shifted and you saw slightly larger batches during tails; that can increase p99 for latency sensitive small prompts. One knob is to set a lower max-batch and tighter batch latency to favor p95 over throughput.
[02:44] Tom Alvarez: can you quantify the delta?
[02:46] Marcus Chen: sure — in Parcelly's sweep: baseline FP16 p95 was ~120ms for the short prompts, INT8 p95 moved to ~132ms (about +12ms), p99 went from ~210ms to ~260ms at peak bursting. FP8 p95 was ~118ms and p99 ~230ms — so FP8 looked better at p95 but worse at p99 compared to FP16 in some windows.
[03:10] Rachel Kim: those numbers match our dashboards. note the p95 bump mattered for some SLAs where client-facing latency needs to be <150ms.
[03:18] Priya Gupta: so operationally if we move to INT8 we might save on cost but risk SLA hits during marketing spikes. We need a fallback strategy.
[03:26] Lena Ortiz: agreed. Typical pattern we recommend is a weighted canary: start 20% traffic on INT8 for non-critical routes, use FP16 fallback on mismatch or when p95 exceeds threshold for a sliding window. Also automatic fallback on quality regression signals — we can wire the eval hooks to your observability if you want.
[03:44] Rachel Kim: that would be good, especially the automated quality gating. how do you see the gating implemented?
[03:49] Marcus Chen: Redwood Optimize can evaluate a sampled subset of responses — we compute score deltas against the golden-set and if the rolling window exceeds configured tolerances we shift traffic back. it's a pegged threshold — e.g. >1% SNR delta or >0.5% exact-match loss for critical intents.
[04:03] Rachel Kim: okay, and about the canary — what about dedicated capacity? we are considering Redwood Dedicated for predictable performance.
[04:09] Lena Ortiz: Dedicated makes sense if you want consistent p99 tails and reserved GPU pools. On Dedicated you can pin the kernel variants and batching policies so tails are more stable; plus we can offer a SLA on latency tiers. However Dedicated pricing will change the cost math versus hosted INT8. We'll send a committed quote after you decide traffic coverage.
[04:28] Tom Alvarez: what about private deployment? we have compliance needs — SOC2, SSO, KMS retention policies and some on-prem requirements for long-term logs.
[04:36] Lena Ortiz: for Private we offer a VPC-deployed control plane or full on-prem. KMS/HSM integrations are supported, audit logs can be configured with a retention policy that meets your requirement, and SAML SSO plus RBAC is standard. We'll schedule a security deep-dive next week to go through the exact mappings you need.
[04:51] Nick Foster: yeah let's do that. also important — can the KV cache be forced FP16 even for INT8 inference to reduce quality regressions?
[04:58] Marcus Chen: yes — runtime supports hybrid caching: keep activations/kv in FP16 while compute kernels use INT8. That adds a bit of memory and a small perf hit but often recovers quality substantially. We saw in your case it reduced the long-context hallucination rate by ~50% with p95 +6ms overhead.
[05:16] Rachel Kim: we also observed a small edge-case where tokenization differences caused misalignment for one of our language-specific prompts — it might be a tokenizer vocab mismatch between the quantized artifact and baseline.
[05:26] Aya Singh: good catch, tokenizer/embedding table quantization sometimes needs re-alignment post-quant. we should run a checksum pass to ensure embeddings are identical pre-quant.
[05:33] Tom Alvarez: action item: we can drop the sample prompts and logs into the shared S3 bucket today.
[05:38] Rachel Kim: yes I'll upload the failing set.
[05:41] Lena Ortiz: excellent. quick note on the perf tuning we tried: Marcus, you did an ablation on batch sizes and num threads right?
[05:47] Marcus Chen: correct — small batch bias for latency critical routes: max-batch 8 and 5ms batch latency cap gave best p95. For throughput-heavy background jobs we used max-batch 64 and 20ms latency cap, which is where INT8 shined — about 1.9x token throughput.
[06:05] Priya Gupta: can you put those recommended config snippets in the runbook?
[06:08] Marcus Chen: yes will add them to the runbook and the spreadsheet.
[06:10] Rachel Kim: one question about evaluation: our human eval set flagged some nuanced policy safety differences in FP8 vs INT8 — FP8 had fewer hallucinations but slightly more verbose safety wrappers. it's subtle. thoughts?
[06:22] Aya Singh: sometimes FP8 introduces softer logits which can push the decoding into more cautious tokens; that may explain the verbosity. This is model- and prompt-dependent. We can surface per-prompt token distribution changes in the spreadsheet to help you decide.
[06:34] Nick Foster: from infra side, if we want to run a 48h throughput test what does Redwood need access to?
[06:39] Lena Ortiz: ideally a temporary VPC peering and a service account with limited scope so our benchmark harness can hit the same endpoints. We'll provide IP ranges and a runbook. Also need permission to pull the anonymized logs for the run.
[06:52] Tom Alvarez: we can do that, will create an IAM role for the test and set up peering.
[06:57] Rachel Kim: one more ask — can you provide a breakdown of cost per million tokens for INT8 vs FP8 vs FP16 on Dedicated? We need that for the finance team.
[07:05] Lena Ortiz: yes we'll produce a delta table — include amortized GPU costs, licensing, and expected savings at your traffic profile. Expect that in the quote.
[07:12] Priya Gupta: any blockers on compliance for Private?
[07:15] Lena Ortiz: none immediate — we'll need the security questionnaire filled and then a follow-up scoping session. Our security docs cover SOC2, ISO, KMS, and audit logs; for on-prem specifics we'll need the network and air-gap constraints.
[07:27] Rachel Kim: ok moving back to the quality numbers — can you speak to how the automatic fallback will surface to our observability and whether it's reversible without losing state?
[07:36] Marcus Chen: yes fallback is stateful at the request-router level: when switching from INT8 to FP16 we preserve KV-cache keys where compatible; for long-context sessions there can be a cold-cache penalty. We recommend doing controlled rollbacks on session boundaries or using the hybrid-KV tactic to minimize state loss.
[07:57] Priya Gupta: what about legal/ procurement timeline for Dedicated? we have procurement blackout weeks in late July.
[08:03] Lena Ortiz: noted. we can aim to have the commercial terms and quotes by end of next week if you want to fast-track. Procurement can review in early August before blackout.
[08:12] Rachel Kim: sounds good. ok let's recap quick so we have clear next steps.
[08:16] Lena Ortiz: recap: Redwood to share eval spreadsheet and raw latency traces; Redwood to produce p95/p99 charts and runbook snippets for batching and hybrid KV; Parcelly to upload failing prompts and grant temporary VPC access for 48h run; schedule security deep-dive for KMS and audit logs; Redwood to send Dedicated cost delta and quote.
[08:36] Tom Alvarez: I'll take the VPC action.
[08:38] Rachel Kim: I'll upload prompts tonight.
[08:40] Lena Ortiz: perfect. any final questions?
[08:43] Nick Foster: maybe one — for the automatic quality gate, what's the expected false-positive rate? we don't want the gate to flip traffic too often.
[08:50] Marcus Chen: it depends on sampling and metric thresholds — typically we tune sample size to get <3% false-positive on our holdout. We'll propose an initial config and you can adjust.
[08:59] Priya Gupta: thanks everyone.
[09:01] Lena Ortiz: thanks all, we'll follow up with the artifacts and calendar invite for the security deep-dive.
[09:06] (meeting ends)
